question: What is the main reason we monitor a child's growth at the clinic?

options.A: To detect growth problems before visible signs appear
options.B: To treat children who already have severe infections
options.C: To vaccinate children against common childhood illnesses
options.D: To provide free food supplies to low-income families

explanation: Spotting small changes in weight or height early lets you step in and help before severe malnutrition sets in. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h1)

question: Why do we track a child's growth over several visits rather than relying on just one measurement?

options.A: It prevents errors made by community health volunteers
options.B: It shows the direction and velocity of growth over time
options.C: It guarantees the child will not contract infectious diseases
options.D: It is required by government health insurance policies

explanation: A single visit only tells you about today. Tracking over time shows the true pattern—whether the child is growing well or falling behind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h1)

question: If a young child has a low height-for-age, what does this usually tell us?
explanation: Height takes time to change, so a low height-for-age points to long-term nutritional challenges or repeated illnesses over time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h2)

question: A child suddenly loses a lot of weight over two weeks. Which measurement will drop first?
explanation: Weight changes fast during short-term illness or food shortages, making weight-for-length our best early warning sign for sudden wasting. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h2)

question: What is the correct tool to measure the length of a 14-month-old child?
explanation: Kids under two can't stand straight yet, so we use a flat measuring board (infantometer) while they lie down. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h3)

question: Why should a nurse adjust the weighing scale to zero before weighing every child?

options.A: To make the scale display readings in kilograms instead of pounds
options.B: To comply with international manufacturer warranties
options.C: To calm the child down before the measurement process begins
options.D: To prevent small errors from accumulating between readings

explanation: Always zeroing your scale clears any leftover weight from the previous patient, keeping your numbers accurate every time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h3)

question: How can a nurse prevent reading errors (parallax errors) when using a weighing scale?

options.A: Reading the scale directly at eye level
options.B: Using a digital scale instead of an analog one
options.C: Weighing the child twice and taking the average
options.D: Calibrating the scale with a known standard weight

explanation: Looking at the dial or screen from above or the side can skew your reading. Always position your eyes straight in front of the display! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h4)

question: When measuring the length of a 10-month-old infant, what should you do with their legs?

options.A: Gently press the knees down so the legs lie flat against the board
options.B: Leave the knees relaxed and bent naturally in a frog position
options.C: Wrap both ankles tightly together with a soft bandage
options.D: Lift the legs upward at a 45-degree angle to stretch the spine

explanation: If the knees are bent, your measurement will be shorter than reality. Gently hold the knees flat against the board for an accurate length. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h4)

question: On a standard WHO growth chart, what does the bottom (horizontal) line represent?
explanation: Think of the horizontal axis as time passing (age), while the vertical axis shows the measurement like weight or height. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h5)

question: What does it mean when a child's plotted dots form a line pointing upward, running parallel to the reference curves?

options.B: Immediate risk of severe acute malnutrition
options.C: An error in the initial birth weight record
options.D: Chronic stunting due to repeated infections

explanation: When the curve follows the expected upward path, it's a great sign that the child is gaining weight and growing steadily! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h5)

question: What does 'growth faltering' look like on a child's growth chart?

options.A: A steady upward curve parallel to reference lines
options.B: Measurements that stay above the median line
options.C: A sudden increase in height over one month
options.D: A flat or downward-sloping growth curve

explanation: Growth faltering happens when weight gain slows down or stops entirely, making the growth line flatten out or dip downwards. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h6)

question: Why is it an urgent concern if a child's weight line crosses downward across Z-score lines?

options.A: It indicates normal seasonal weight loss in toddlers
options.B: It means the mother has stopped bringing the child to the clinic
options.C: It shows an active deterioration in nutritional status
options.D: It proves the weighing scale was broken during the visit

explanation: Crossing downward means the child is actively losing ground toward malnutrition and needs quick clinical attention. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a common cause of growth faltering in infants?
explanation: Normal baby movement doesn't cause faltering. Illness, infections, and poor feeding are the real culprits behind slowed growth. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h7)

question: How do recurring illnesses like malaria lead to childhood malnutrition?

options.A: By directly destroying the child's bone marrow and skeleton
options.B: By changing the color of breast milk in the mother's body
options.C: By forcing the child to sleep longer hours during the day
options.D: By increasing nutrient demand while reducing the child's appetite

explanation: Fever and sickness make the body burn more energy, but sick kids usually don't want to eat. That combination leads straight to weight loss. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h7)

question: What is the best way to start counselling a mother whose child is experiencing growth faltering?

options.A: Tell the mother to stop coming to the clinic until next year
options.B: Ask open-ended questions about recent feeding and illness
options.C: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child properly
options.D: Write a prescription for expensive imported vitamin supplements

explanation: Great nursing starts with empathy and listening. Ask gentle, open questions to understand what's happening at home without judging. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h8)

question: A toddler is showing growth faltering. What is the most practical nutrition advice to give the mother?

options.A: Stop all breastfeeding immediately and switch entirely to cow milk
options.B: Only feed the child imported baby cereals bought from supermarkets
options.C: Reduce the number of daily meals to allow the child's stomach to rest
options.D: Use available local food items to make nutrient-dense meals given more frequently

explanation: Keep advice practical! Recommend affordable, locally available foods that the family can easily prepare and feed the child more often. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h8)
